jobs.description:
Join the team responsible for the High Throughput Compute systems at the heart of CERN's data processing!

Are you a recent graduate with an interest in large-scale computing, automation, and infrastructure technologies? Would you like to develop your skills while contributing to the evolution of the computing infrastructure supporting the High-Luminosity LHC?

As a member of the team responsible for the batch service and configuration management of IT services, you will have the opportunity to experience a varied role, from helping to automate the delivery of compute, to self healing infrastructure, to evolving the toolset that the IT department uses to manage its services.

The Compute and Devices (CD) group in CERN IT provides a wide range of compute services, all the way from end user devices, through cloud infrastructure-as-a- Service, machine-learning, Kubernetes, configuration management, batch and HPC computing at CERN, together with a set of services that support the whole WLCG.

As a member of the Compute and Configuration (CC) section of the CD group, you will join a team of engineers focusing on services supporting the physics community. We run the compute facility that comprises approximately 20% of the WLCG, using tools such as Puppet, OpenStack and Kubernetes to manage batch systems running HTCondor, HPC systems running SLURM, and the support services keeping everything glued together.

If you enjoy solving complex technical challenges, contributing to open-source software, and working with infrastructure at scale, come join us!
 Your responsibilities

• Help manage the fleet of 400k+ cores complete lifecycle from CI provisioning through automated and AI enhanced maintenance.

• Help keep us ahead of LLM enhanced security threats with monitoring.

• Suggest, test, and deploy configuration changes on a large scale to production.

• Contribute to the operation and maintenance of the current configuration management infrastructure, including Foreman, Puppet and OpenVox components.

• Contribute to the development and maintenance of Terraform/OpenTofu modules used to provision and configure the supporting infrastructure.

• Improve the quality of the configuration code through testing, validation, code review and standardisation.
 Your profile

• Experience administering or working with Linux systems in a server or data centre environment.

• Experience writing scripts or applications for automation or system tasks.

• Experience with configuration management tools such as Puppet or Ansible is a plus.

• Experience with container technologies, CI/CD systems or Infrastructure-as-Code tools is a plus.
 Skills

• Knowledge of Linux, programming or scripting languages such as Python or Go.

• Familiarity with git for distributed version control is highly desirable.

• Knowledge of configuration management tools such as Puppet or Ansible is desirable.

• Infrastructure as Code tools such as Terraform or OpenTofu would be a plus.

• Any knowledge of batch systems such as HTCondor, SLURM or kueue would be a plus.

• Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.
 Eligibility criteria:

• You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State .

• By the application deadline, you have a maximum of two years of professional experience since graduation in Computer Science (or a related field) and your highest educational qualification is either a Bachelor's or Master's degree .

• You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.

• Applicants without University degree are not eligible.

• Applicants with a PhD are not eligible.

Job closing date: 08.10.2026 at 23:59 CEST.
 Contract duration: 24 months, with a possible extension up to 36 months maximum.
 Working hours: 40 hours per week
 Job flexibility: Hybrid
 Target start date: 01-December-2026
 This position involves:

• Stand-by duty, when required by the needs of the Organization.

• Work during nights, Sundays and official holidays, when required by the needs of the Organization.
 Job reference: IT-CD-CC-2026-223-GRAE
 Field of work: Information Technologies
 Benchmark job: 200020 - Computing Engineer

Global Benefits

• A monthly net stipend of either 5266 or 5793 Swiss Francs per month depending on your degree.

• 30 days of paid leave per year plus 2 weeks annual closure.

• Coverage by CERN’s comprehensive health insurance scheme (for yourself, your spouse and children), and membership of the CERN Pension Fund.

• Family, child and infant monthly allowances depending on your individual circumstances.

• A relocation package (installation grant and travel expenses) depending on your individual circumstances.

• Possibility to extend your contract up to 36 months.

• On-the-job and formal training including language classes.
 Overview of CERN - Discover a world where the impossible is made possible!
 At CERN, the European Organization for Nuclear Research, we are pushing the frontiers of science and technology. Our groundbreaking work brings together not only physicists but also a diverse range of professionals from engineering, technical, scientific, and administrative fields. Together, we foster an environment where innovation and collaboration thrive.
 Every day, we face exciting new challenges and opportunities to contribute to cutting-edge research that shapes our understanding of the universe. We meet these challenges through the diverse perspectives within our teams, ensuring every contribution is valued and driving our shared sense of inclusion and purpose. Diversity is a core value of CERN since its foundation, and it remains central to our mission and continued success.
 If you are ready to be part of a dynamic, inclusive community pushing the boundaries of knowledge, CERN is the place where your curiosity and skills can thrive. Be part of our mission to uncover what lies at the heart of the universe! TAKE PART!
 More information about us, here: careers.cern

descriptionByLocale.it:
Unisciti al team responsabile dei sistemi High Throughput Compute nel cuore dell'elaborazione dei dati del CERN!

Sei un recente laureato con un interesse per le tecnologie di calcolo, automazione e infrastrutture su larga scala? Vorresti sviluppare le tue competenze, contribuendo all'evoluzione dell'infrastruttura informatica che supporta l'High-Luminosity LHC?

Come membro del team responsabile per il servizio in batch e la gestione della configurazione dei servizi IT, avrete l'opportunità di sperimentare un ruolo vario, dall'aiutare a automatizzare la consegna della computazione, all'infrastruttura di autoguarigione, all'evoluzione degli strumenti che il reparto IT utilizza per gestire i suoi servizi.

Il gruppo Compute and Devices (CD) in CERN IT offre una vasta gamma di servizi di calcolo, che vanno dai dispositivi degli utenti finali, attraverso infrastrutture cloud-as-a- Service, machine-learning, Kubernetes, gestione della configurazione, elaborazione batch e HPC al CERN, insieme ad una serie di servizi che supportano l'intero WLCG.

Come membro della sezione Compute and Configuration (CC) del gruppo CD, si unirà a un team di ingegneri che si concentrano sui servizi che supportano la comunità fisica. Eseguiamo la struttura di calcolo che comprende circa il 20% del WLCG, utilizzando strumenti come Puppet, OpenStack e Kubernetes per gestire i sistemi batch in esecuzione HTCondor, sistemi HPC in esecuzione SLURM, e i servizi di supporto mantenendo tutto incollato insieme.

Se ti piace risolvere complesse sfide tecniche, contribuire al software open source, e lavorare con l'infrastruttura in scala, unirsi a noi!
Le tue responsabilità

• Aiuta a gestire la flotta di 400k+ cores completo ciclo di vita da CI provisioning attraverso la manutenzione automatizzata e potenziata AI.

• Aiuta a tenerci davanti alle minacce di sicurezza potenziate LLM con il monitoraggio.

• Suggerisci, testa e implementa le modifiche di configurazione su larga scala alla produzione.

• Contribuisci al funzionamento e alla manutenzione dell'attuale infrastruttura di gestione della configurazione, inclusi i componenti Foreman, Puppet e OpenVox.

• Contribuisci allo sviluppo e alla manutenzione dei moduli Terraform/OpenTofu utilizzati per fornire e configurare l'infrastruttura di supporto.

• Migliorare la qualità del codice di configurazione tramite test, validazione, revisione del codice e standardizzazione.
Il tuo profilo

• Esperienza di gestione o di lavoro con sistemi Linux in un ambiente server o data center.

• Sperimenta gli script di scrittura o le applicazioni per l'automazione o le attività di sistema.

• Esperienza con strumenti di gestione della configurazione come Puppet o Ansible è un plus.

• Esperienza con tecnologie per container, sistemi CI/CD o strumenti Infrastructure-as-Code è un plus.
Competenze

• Conoscenza di Linux, linguaggi di programmazione o scripting come Python o Go.

• La familiarità con git per il controllo di versione distribuito è altamente auspicabile.

• La conoscenza di strumenti di gestione della configurazione come Puppet o Ansible è auspicabile.

• Infrastrutture come strumenti di codice come Terraform o OpenTofu sarebbe un plus.

• Qualsiasi conoscenza di sistemi batch come HTCondor, SLURM o kueue sarebbe un plus.

• Parlato e scritto inglese, con un impegno per imparare il francese.
Criteri di ammissibilità:

• Sei un cittadino di uno Stato membro del CERN o di uno Stato membro associato .

• Con la scadenza dell'applicazione, si dispone di un massimo di due anni di esperienza professionale dalla laurea in Informatica (o un campo correlato) e la vostra più alta qualifica educativa è sia una laurea o master.

• Non hai mai avuto un contratto di laurea o di socio del CERN.

• I candidati senza laurea non sono ammissibili.

• I candidati con un dottorato non sono ammissibili.

Data di chiusura del lavoro: 08.10.2026 alle 23:59 CEST.
Durata del contratto: 24 mesi, con una possibile estensione fino a 36 mesi massimo.
Orario di lavoro: 40 ore settimanali
Flessibilità del lavoro: ibrido
Data di inizio obiettivo: 01-dicembre-2026
Questa posizione comporta:

• In piedi, quando richiesto dalle esigenze dell'Organizzazione.

• Lavorare durante le notti, la domenica e le vacanze ufficiali, quando richiesto dalle esigenze dell'Organizzazione.
Riferimento del lavoro: IT-CD-CC-2026-223-GRAE
Campo di lavoro: Tecnologie dell'informazione
Lavoro Benchmark: 200020 - Ingegnere di calcolo

Vantaggi globali

• Una spesa netta mensile di 5266 o 5793 franchi svizzeri al mese a seconda della laurea.

• 30 giorni di congedo retribuito all'anno più 2 settimane di chiusura annuale.

• Copertura dell’assicurazione sanitaria completa del CERN (per te, il tuo coniuge e i tuoi figli) e dell’iscrizione al CERN Pension Fund.

• Indennità mensili di famiglia, bambino e bambino a seconda delle circostanze individuali.

• Un pacchetto di trasferimento (concessione di installazione e spese di viaggio) a seconda delle vostre circostanze individuali.

• Possibilità di estendere il contratto fino a 36 mesi.

• On-the-job e formazione formale, comprese le lezioni di lingua.
Panoramica del CERN - Scopri un mondo in cui l'impossibile è reso possibile!
Al CERN, l'Organizzazione europea per la ricerca nucleare, stiamo spingendo le frontiere della scienza e della tecnologia. Il nostro lavoro innovativo riunisce non solo i fisici, ma anche una vasta gamma di professionisti provenienti da settori ingegneristici, tecnici, scientifici e amministrativi. Insieme, promuoviamo un ambiente in cui l'innovazione e la collaborazione prosperano.
Ogni giorno affrontiamo nuove entusiasmanti sfide e opportunità per contribuire alla ricerca all'avanguardia che plasma la nostra comprensione dell'universo. Incontriamo queste sfide attraverso le diverse prospettive all'interno dei nostri team, assicurando che ogni contributo sia valutato e guida il nostro senso condiviso di inclusione e scopo. La diversità è un valore fondamentale del CERN fin dalla sua fondazione, e rimane centrale per la nostra missione e il successo continuo.
Se siete pronti a far parte di una comunità dinamica e inclusiva che spinge i confini della conoscenza, il CERN è il luogo in cui la vostra curiosità e abilità possono prosperare. Fate parte della nostra missione per scoprire cosa sta nel cuore dell'universo! Partita!
Maggiori informazioni su di noi, qui: careers.cern

Schließen Sie sich dem Team an, das für die Hochdurchsatz-Compute-Systeme im Herzen der Datenverarbeitung des CERN verantwortlich ist!

Sind Sie ein neuer Absolvent mit Interesse an groß angelegten Computer-, Automatisierungs- und Infrastrukturtechnologien? Möchten Sie Ihre Fähigkeiten entwickeln und gleichzeitig zur Entwicklung der Computerinfrastruktur beitragen, die den LHC mit hoher Luminosität unterstützt?

Als Mitglied des Teams, das für den Batch-Service und das Konfigurationsmanagement von IT-Services verantwortlich ist, haben Sie die Möglichkeit, eine abwechslungsreiche Rolle zu spielen, von der Unterstützung bei der Automatisierung der Bereitstellung von Computern über die Selbstheilungsinfrastruktur bis hin zur Entwicklung des Toolsets, das die IT-Abteilung zur Verwaltung ihrer Dienste verwendet.

Die Compute and Devices (CD) -Gruppe in CERN IT bietet eine breite Palette von Compute-Services, von Endbenutzergeräten über Cloud-Infrastruktur-as-a-Service, Machine-Learning, Kubernetes, Konfigurationsmanagement, Batch- und HPC-Computing am CERN, zusammen mit einer Reihe von Diensten, die das gesamte WLCG unterstützen.

Als Mitglied des Bereichs Compute and Configuration (CC) der CD-Gruppe treten Sie einem Team von Ingenieuren bei, das sich auf Dienste konzentriert, die die Physik-Community unterstützen. Wir betreiben die Rechenanlage, die etwa 20% des WLCG umfasst, mit Tools wie Puppet, OpenStack und Kubernetes, um Batch-Systeme mit HTCondor, HPC-Systeme mit SLURM und die Support-Services zu verwalten, die alles zusammenhalten.

Wenn Sie gerne komplexe technische Herausforderungen lösen, zu Open-Source-Software beitragen und mit Infrastruktur in großem Maßstab arbeiten, kommen Sie zu uns!

• Helfen Sie mit, die Flotte von 400k+ Kernen kompletten Lebenszyklus von CI-Bereitstellung durch automatisierte und KI-verbesserte Wartung zu verwalten.

• Vertrautheit mit git für verteilte Versionskontrolle ist sehr wünschenswert.

• Infrastruktur als Code-Tools wie Terraform oder OpenTofu wären ein Plus.

Rejoignez l'équipe responsable des systèmes de calcul à haut débit au cœur du traitement des données du CERN !

Êtes-vous récemment diplômé avec un intérêt pour l'informatique à grande échelle, l'automatisation et les technologies d'infrastructure? Souhaitez-vous développer vos compétences tout en contribuant à l'évolution de l'infrastructure informatique qui soutient le LHC à haute luminosité?

En tant que membre de l'équipe responsable du service par lots et de la gestion de la configuration des services de TI, vous aurez l'occasion de faire l'expérience d'un rôle varié, allant de l'automatisation de la prestation du calcul, à l'autogestion de l'infrastructure, à l'évolution des outils utilisés par le service de TI pour gérer ses services.

Le groupe Compute and Devices (CD) du CERN IT offre une large gamme de services de calcul, depuis les appareils utilisateurs finaux jusqu'à l'infrastructure cloud comme service, l'apprentissage automatique, Kubernetes, la gestion de configuration, le calcul par lots et HPC au CERN, ainsi qu'un ensemble de services qui prennent en charge l'ensemble du WLCG.

En tant que membre de la section Calcul et configuration (CC) du groupe CD, vous rejoindrez une équipe d'ingénieurs axée sur les services de soutien à la communauté physique. Nous gérons l'installation de calcul qui comprend environ 20% de la WLCG, en utilisant des outils tels que Puppet, OpenStack et Kubernetes pour gérer les systèmes par lots fonctionnant avec HTCondor, les systèmes HPC fonctionnant avec SLURM, et les services de soutien gardant tout collé ensemble.

Si vous aimez résoudre des défis techniques complexes, contribuer au logiciel open-source et travailler avec l'infrastructure à l'échelle, venez nous rejoindre!
Vos responsabilités

• Aider à gérer le parc de cœurs de 400k+ à mener à bien le cycle de vie de la fourniture de l'IC par une maintenance automatisée et améliorée par l'IA.

• Aidez-nous à nous maintenir en avance sur les menaces de sécurité accrues de la LLM avec la surveillance.

• Suggérer, tester et déployer des changements de configuration à grande échelle à la production.

• Contribuer à l'exploitation et à l'entretien de l'infrastructure de gestion de configuration actuelle, y compris les composants Foreman, Puppet et OpenVox.

• Contribuer au développement et à l'entretien des modules Terraform/OpenTofu utilisés pour fournir et configurer l'infrastructure de soutien.

• Améliorer la qualité du code de configuration grâce à des essais, à la validation, à la révision du code et à la normalisation.
Votre profil

• Expérience d'administration ou de travail avec les systèmes Linux dans un environnement serveur ou datacenter.

• Expérience d'écriture de scripts ou d'applications pour des tâches d'automatisation ou de système.

• Expérience avec des outils de gestion de configuration comme Puppet ou Ansible est un plus.

• Expérience des technologies de conteneurs, des systèmes CI/CD ou des outils Infrastructure-as-Code est un plus.
Compétences

• Connaissance de Linux, programmation ou langage de script comme Python ou Go.

• Familiarité avec git pour le contrôle de version distribuée est hautement souhaitable.

• La connaissance d'outils de gestion de configuration comme la marionnette ou Ansible est souhaitable.

• L'infrastructure comme les outils Code comme Terraform ou OpenTofu serait un plus.

• Help manage and assess the fire safety compliance of materials used in the CMS Phase II Upgrade Projects, including follow-up risk assessments for potentially non-compliant materials.

Nell'ambito del team di coordinamento tecnico per l'esperimento CMS presso il Large Hadron Collider (LHC), si unirà al team di sicurezza e si familiarizzerà con i sistemi e gli allarmi di sicurezza CERN e CMS, i processi di identificazione e valutazione dei rischi, nonché con gli strumenti di infrastruttura e calcolo CMS.
Le tue responsabilità

• Sostenere il CMS LEXGLIMOS (Large Experiment Group Leader in Matters of Safety), lavorando a stretto contatto con il team di coordinamento tecnico CMS e contribuendo all'attuazione degli obiettivi di sicurezza del CERN all'interno del CMS e definendo le priorità e le tempistiche associate.

• Contribuire alla stesura e alla revisione delle valutazioni e delle procedure di rischio per progetti, lavori, aree e attività, nonché all'aggiornamento del File di Sicurezza associato, in particolare a sostegno dell'aggiornamento CMS LS3.

• Aiuta a gestire e valutare la conformità della sicurezza antincendio dei materiali utilizzati nei progetti di aggiornamento CMS Phase II, comprese le valutazioni dei rischi di follow-up per materiali potenzialmente non conformi.

• Eseguire analisi degli incidenti e seguire l'attuazione di azioni di sicurezza e misure di sicurezza per sostenere il miglioramento continuo.

• Sostenere le attività di preparazione di emergenza all'interno del CMS, compreso il coordinamento e l'organizzazione di evacuazioni pianificate.
Il tuo profilo

• Esperienza di base in ingegneria (sicurezza, industriale, meccanica, o un campo correlato).

• Esposizione a ambienti di laboratorio, workshop o tecnici.

• Esperienza iniziale (attraverso progetti accademici, stage o attività simili) nella valutazione del rischio, identificazione dei rischi, sicurezza antincendio e relative misure di sicurezza.

• Familiarità con gestione dei dati, reporting e documentazione tecnica.

• Esperienza di lavoro in progetti multidisciplinari o basati su team.
Competenze

• Esperienza iniziale nella gestione della sicurezza e del rischio professionale, compresa la valutazione delle attività sul posto di lavoro, l'identificazione dei rischi e l'analisi dei rischi.

• Conoscenza dei progetti relativi alla sicurezza in strutture industriali o scientifiche complesse.

• Forte capacità di comunicazione scritta e verbale, con la capacità di collaborare efficacemente con team e stakeholder multidisciplinari.

• Capacità di redigere documentazione di sicurezza e fornire presentazioni orali in almeno una delle due lingue ufficiali del CERN (inglese o francese).

• Proattivo, organizzato e orientato al dettaglio, con la capacità di gestire più compiti e lavorare sia indipendentemente che come parte di un team.

• Forte capacità analitiche e problem solving, con un forte interesse per la sicurezza, l'ingegneria e la consegna di progetti.

• Parlato e scritto inglese o francese, con un impegno per imparare l'altra lingua.
Criteri di ammissibilità:

• Sei un cittadino di uno Stato membro del CERN o di uno Stato membro associato .

• Con la scadenza dell'applicazione, si dispone di un massimo di due anni di esperienza professionale dalla laurea in Sicurezza o Ingegneria Industriale (o un campo correlato) e la vostra più alta qualifica educativa è sia una laurea o master.

• Non hai mai avuto un contratto di laurea o di socio del CERN.

• I candidati senza laurea non sono ammissibili.

• I candidati con un dottorato non sono ammissibili.

Panoramica del CERN - Scopri un mondo in cui l'impossibile è reso possibile!
Al CERN, l'Organizzazione europea per la ricerca nucleare, stiamo spingendo le frontiere della scienza e della tecnologia. Il nostro lavoro innovativo riunisce non solo i fisici, ma anche una vasta gamma di professionisti provenienti da settori ingegneristici, tecnici, scientifici e amministrativi. Insieme, promuoviamo un ambiente in cui l'innovazione e la collaborazione prosperano.

descriptionByLocale.en:
As part of the Technical Coordination team for the CMS Experiment at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), you will join the Safety Team and familiarise yourself with CERN and CMS safety systems and alarms, hazard identification and risk assessment processes, as well as CMS infrastructure and computing tools.
Your responsibilities

• Support the CMS LEXGLIMOS (Large Experiment Group Leader in Matters of Safety), working closely with the CMS Technical Coordination team and contributing to implementing CERN's safety objectives within CMS and defining the associated priorities and timelines.

• Contribute to drafting and reviewing risk assessments and procedures for projects, works, areas and activities, and to updating the associated Safety File, particularly in support of the LS3 CMS upgrade.

• Help manage and assess the fire safety compliance of materials used in the CMS Phase II Upgrade Projects, including follow-up risk assessments for potentially non-compliant materials.

• Perform incident analyses and follow up on the implementation of safety actions and safety measures to support continuous improvement.

• Support emergency preparedness activities within CMS, including the coordination and organisation of planned evacuations.
Your profile

• Basic experience in engineering (safety, industrial, mechanical, or a related field).

• Exposure to laboratory, workshop, or technical environments.

• Initial experience (through academic projects, internships, or similar activities) in risk assessment, hazard identification, fire safety, and related safety measures.

• Familiarity with data handling, reporting, and technical documentation.

• Experience working in multidisciplinary or team-based projects.
Skills

• Initial experience in occupational safety and risk management, including assessing workplace activities, identifying hazards, and analysing risks.

• Knowledge of safety-related projects in complex industrial or scientific facilities.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with multidisciplinary teams and stakeholders.

• Ability to draft safety documentation and deliver oral presentations in at least one of CERN's two official languages (English or French).

• Proactive, organised, and detail-oriented, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and work both independently and as part of a team.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a keen interest in safety, engineering, and project delivery.

• Spoken and written English or French, with a commitment to learn the other language.
Eligibility criteria:

• You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State .

• By the application deadline, you have a maximum of two years of professional experience since graduation in Safety or Industrial Engineering (or a related field) and your highest educational qualification is either a Bachelor's or Master's degree .

• You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.

• Applicants without University degree are not eligible.

• Applicants with a PhD are not eligible.

Job closing date: 08.10.2026 at 23:59 CEST.
Contract duration: 24 months, with a possible extension up to 36 months maximum.
Job flexibility: Fully Onsite
Target start date: 01-January-2027
This position involves:

• Work in Radiation Areas.

• Interventions in underground installations.

• Residence in the immediate vicinity of the Organization's installations.

• A valid driving licence.

• Work during nights, Sundays and official holidays, when required by the needs of the Organization.

• Exposure to electromagnetic fields under certain exposure conditions.

descriptionByLocale.de:
Als Teil des Technical Coordination Teams für das CMS Experiment am Large Hadron Collider (LHC) werden Sie Teil des Safety Teams und machen sich mit CERN- und CMS-Sicherheitssystemen und Alarmen, Gefahrenerkennungs- und Risikobewertungsprozessen sowie CMS-Infrastruktur und Computer-Tools vertraut.
Ihre Verantwortung

• Unterstützen Sie das CMS LEXGLIMOS (Large Experiment Group Leader in Matters of Safety), arbeiten Sie eng mit dem CMS Technical Coordination Team zusammen und tragen Sie zur Umsetzung der CERN-Sicherheitsziele innerhalb des CMS bei und definieren Sie die damit verbundenen Prioritäten und Zeitpläne.

• Beitrag zur Erstellung und Überprüfung von Risikobewertungen und Verfahren für Projekte, Arbeiten, Bereiche und Aktivitäten sowie zur Aktualisierung der zugehörigen Sicherheitsdatei, insbesondere zur Unterstützung des Upgrades des LS3 CMS.

• Unterstützung bei der Verwaltung und Bewertung der Brandschutzkonformität von Materialien, die in den CMS Phase-II-Upgrade-Projekten verwendet werden, einschließlich Folgerisikobewertungen für potenziell nicht konforme Materialien.

• Durchführung von Störfallanalysen und Weiterverfolgung der Umsetzung von Sicherheitsmaßnahmen und Sicherheitsmaßnahmen zur Unterstützung der kontinuierlichen Verbesserung.

• Unterstützung von Notfallvorsorgeaktivitäten innerhalb des CMS, einschließlich der Koordination und Organisation geplanter Evakuierungen.
Dein Profil

• Grundkenntnisse im Ingenieurwesen (Sicherheit, Industrie, Mechanik oder ein verwandtes Gebiet).

• Exposition gegenüber Labor, Werkstatt oder technischen Umgebungen.

• Erste Erfahrungen (durch akademische Projekte, Praktika oder ähnliche Aktivitäten) in der Risikobewertung, Gefahrenermittlung, Brandschutz und damit verbundenen Sicherheitsmaßnahmen.

• Vertrautheit mit Datenverarbeitung, Berichterstattung und technischer Dokumentation.

• Erfahrung in multidisziplinären oder teambasierten Projekten.
Fähigkeiten

• Erste Erfahrungen im Bereich Arbeitssicherheit und Risikomanagement, einschließlich der Bewertung von Arbeitsplatzaktivitäten, der Ermittlung von Gefahren und der Analyse von Risiken.

• Kenntnisse über sicherheitsrelevante Projekte in komplexen industriellen oder wissenschaftlichen Einrichtungen.

• Starke schriftliche und mündliche Kommunikationsfähigkeiten mit der Fähigkeit, effektiv mit multidisziplinären Teams und Stakeholdern zusammenzuarbeiten.

• Fähigkeit, Sicherheitsdokumentationen zu erstellen und mündliche Präsentationen in mindestens einer der beiden Amtssprachen des CERN (Englisch oder Französisch) zu halten.

• Proaktiv, organisiert und detailorientiert, mit der Fähigkeit, mehrere Aufgaben zu verwalten und sowohl unabhängig als auch als Teil eines Teams zu arbeiten.

• Starke analytische und problemlösende Fähigkeiten, mit einem großen Interesse an Sicherheit, Engineering und Projektabwicklung.

• Gesprochen und geschrieben Englisch oder Französisch, mit der Verpflichtung, die andere Sprache zu lernen.
Förderkriterien:

• Sie sind Staatsangehöriger eines CERN-Mitglieds oder assoziierten Mitgliedstaats.

• Bis zum Bewerbungsschluss haben Sie seit dem Abschluss in Safety oder Industrial Engineering (oder einem verwandten Bereich) maximal zwei Jahre Berufserfahrung und Ihre höchste Bildungsqualifikation ist entweder ein Bachelor- oder Master-Abschluss.

• Sie hatten noch nie einen CERN-Stipendiaten- oder Absolventenvertrag.

• Bewerber ohne Hochschulabschluss sind nicht förderfähig.

• Bewerber mit einem PhD sind nicht förderfähig.

Bei CERN, der Europäischen Organisation für Kernforschung, erweitern wir die Grenzen von Wissenschaft und Technologie. Dans le cadre de l'équipe de coordination technique pour l'expérience du CMS au grand collisionneur de hadron (LHC), vous rejoindrez l'équipe de sécurité et vous familiariserez avec les systèmes de sécurité et les alarmes du CERN et du CMS, les processus d'identification des risques et d'évaluation des risques, ainsi que l'infrastructure du CMS et les outils informatiques.
Vos responsabilités

• Soutenir le CMS LEXGLIMOS (Grand chef de groupe expérimental en matière de sécurité), travailler en étroite collaboration avec l'équipe de coordination technique du CMS et contribuer à la mise en oeuvre des objectifs de sécurité du CERN au sein du CMS et à la définition des priorités et des échéanciers connexes.

• Contribuer à la rédaction et à l'examen des évaluations des risques et des procédures pour les projets, les travaux, les domaines et les activités, et à la mise à jour du dossier de sécurité connexe, particulièrement à l'appui de la mise à niveau du SGC LS3.

• Aider à gérer et à évaluer la conformité en matière de sécurité incendie des matériaux utilisés dans les projets de modernisation de la phase II de la SGC, y compris les évaluations de suivi des risques pour les matériaux potentiellement non conformes.

• Effectuer des analyses d'incidents et assurer le suivi de la mise en œuvre des actions de sécurité et des mesures de sécurité pour soutenir l'amélioration continue.

• Soutenir les activités de préparation aux situations d'urgence au sein de la CMS, y compris la coordination et l'organisation des évacuations prévues.
Votre profil

• Expérience de base en ingénierie (sécurité, industrie, mécanique ou domaine connexe).

• Exposition à des environnements de laboratoire, d'atelier ou techniques.

• Expérience initiale (au moyen de projets universitaires, de stages ou d'activités semblables) dans l'évaluation des risques, l'identification des dangers, la sécurité incendie et les mesures de sécurité connexes.

• Connaissance du traitement des données, des rapports et de la documentation technique.

• Expérience de travail dans des projets multidisciplinaires ou en équipe.
Compétences

• Expérience initiale en matière de sécurité au travail et de gestion des risques, y compris l'évaluation des activités sur le lieu de travail, l'identification des dangers et l'analyse des risques.

• Connaissance des projets liés à la sécurité dans des installations industrielles ou scientifiques complexes.

• Fortes compétences en communication écrite et verbale, avec la capacité de collaborer efficacement avec les équipes multidisciplinaires et les intervenants.

• Capacité de rédiger des documents sur la sécurité et de présenter des exposés oraux dans au moins une des deux langues officielles du CERN (anglais ou français).

• Proactive, organisée et axée sur le détail, avec la capacité de gérer plusieurs tâches et de travailler à la fois indépendamment et en équipe.

• Fortes compétences en analyse et en résolution de problèmes, avec un vif intérêt pour la sécurité, l'ingénierie et la réalisation de projets.

• Anglais ou français parlé et écrit, avec un engagement à apprendre l'autre langue.

Ti unirai a un team responsabile dello sviluppo e dell'ottimizzazione di soluzioni hardware e software per sistemi di controllo, protezione e sicurezza utilizzati nelle strutture sperimentali del CERN. In questo ruolo, contribuirai al funzionamento e all'affidabilità dei sistemi magnetici degli esperimenti LHC, tra cui ATLAS, CMS, ALICE e LHCb, così come altre infrastrutture critiche. Sarete coinvolti nella progettazione, realizzazione e manutenzione di sistemi elettrici a bassa tensione, lavorando a stretto contatto con ingegneri, tecnici e fisici in un ambiente multidisciplinare.
Le tue responsabilità

• Progettazione e documentare sistemi di potenza e controllo a bassa tensione per la sicurezza, il controllo e l'infrastruttura ausiliaria.

• Partecipa all'implementazione, alla sperimentazione e alla messa in servizio di sistemi elettrici per futuri aggiornamenti LHC.

• Contribuire allo sviluppo e alla convalida di circuiti elettrici per applicazioni di controllo e protezione.

• Collabora con fisici, ingegneri e tecnici per sviluppare soluzioni tecniche affidabili ed efficienti.

• Produce documentazione tecnica e supporta il funzionamento di sistemi critici.
Il tuo profilo

• Esperienza di lavoro su ingegneria elettrica, automazione o progetti tecnici.

• Esposizione alla progettazione e documentazione dei circuiti elettrici.

• Esperienza utilizzando strumenti software di ingegneria per la progettazione elettrica (ad esempio EPLAN o equivalente).

• Esperienza con test di laboratorio, attività di messa in servizio o risoluzione dei problemi.

• Partecipazione a progetti tecnici collaborativi che coinvolgono più stakeholder.
Competenze

• Conoscenza dei sistemi di distribuzione e controllo a bassa tensione.

• Capacità di leggere e interpretare gli schemi elettrici e la documentazione tecnica.

• Conoscenza di base dei sistemi PLC, strumentazione e controllo industriale.

• Forte capacità analitiche e di problem solving.

• Buone capacità di comunicazione e la capacità di lavorare efficacemente in team multidisciplinari.

descriptionByLocale.en:
You will join a team responsible for developing and optimising hardware and software solutions for control, protection and safety systems used in CERN's experimental facilities. In this role, you will contribute to the operation and reliability of the magnet systems of the LHC experiments, including ATLAS, CMS, ALICE and LHCb, as well as other critical infrastructure. You will be involved in the design, implementation and maintenance of low-voltage electrical systems, working closely with engineers, technicians and physicists in a multidisciplinary environment.
Your responsibilities

• Design and document low-voltage power and control systems for magnet safety, control and auxiliary infrastructure.

• Participate in the implementation, testing and commissioning of electrical systems for future LHC upgrades.

• Contribute to the development and validation of electrical circuits for control and protection applications.

• Collaborate with physicists, engineers and technicians to develop reliable and efficient technical solutions.

• Produce technical documentation and support the operation of critical systems.
Your profile

• Experience working on electrical engineering, automation or technical projects.

• Exposure to electrical circuit design and documentation.

• Experience using engineering software tools for electrical design (e.g. EPLAN or equivalent).

• Experience with laboratory testing, commissioning or troubleshooting activities.

• Participation in collaborative technical projects involving multiple stakeholders.
Skills

• Knowledge of low-voltage power distribution and control systems.

• Ability to read and interpret electrical schematics and technical documentation.

• Basic knowledge of PLCs, instrumentation and industrial control systems.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

• Good communication skills and the ability to work effectively in multidisciplinary teams.

• Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.
Eligibility criteria:

• You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State .

• By the application deadline, you have a maximum of two years of professional experience since graduation in Electrical Technical Engineering (or a related field) and your highest educational qualification is either a Bachelor's or Master's degree .

• You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.

• Applicants without University degree are not eligible.

• Applicants with a PhD are not eligible.

Job closing date: 11.10.2026 at 23:59 CEST.
Contract duration: 24 months, with a possible extension up to 36 months maximum.
Working hours: 40 hours per week
Job flexibility: Fully Onsite
Target start date: 01-December-2026
This position involves:

• Participation in a regular stand-by duty, including nights, Sundays and official holidays.

• Work in Radiation Areas.

• Interventions in underground installations.

• Residence in the immediate vicinity of the Organization's installations.

• A valid driving licence.

• Stand-by duty, when required by the needs of the Organization.

• Exposure to electromagnetic fields under certain exposure conditions.
Given the occupational health risks associated with this position, the selected candidate must obtain medical clearance before a contract offer is confirmed.

Global Benefits

• A monthly net stipend of either 5266 or 5793 Swiss Francs per month depending on your degree.

• 30 days of paid leave per year plus 2 weeks annual closure.

• Coverage by CERN’s comprehensive health insurance scheme (for yourself, your spouse and children), and membership of the CERN Pension Fund.

At CERN, the European Organization for Nuclear Research, we are pushing the frontiers of science and technology. jobs.description:
Introduction
 The Engineering Department (EN) provides CERN with the Engineering expertise, Infrastructure Systems and Technical Coordination necessary for the design, installation, operation, maintenance and dismantling phases of the CERN accelerator complex and its experimental facilities.

The position is within the Transport and Handling Engineering Group (EN-THE), responsible for preparing, organising and coordinating all transport and handling operations for the CERN accelerators and experiments. The Group also manages the transport of thousands of conventional and unconventional items, chemical and radioactive products each year.

As a Transport and Handling Specialist in EN-THE, you will be part of the Heavy Handling (EN-HE-HH) Section, which is in charge for organising and supervising transport, handling and lifting operations at CERNs accelerators complex, experimental areas and industrial buildings both underground and in surface premises.
 Functions
 As a Transport and Handling Specialist in the EN-THE-HH Section, you will be part of a team of 10 people (technical engineers and technicians) in charge of:

• Coordinating transport and handling operations for the Accelerator complex, Experiments, and surface premises.

• Coordinating and planning meetings to evaluate technical and resource needs.

• Assessing and proposing possible handling and transport solutions.

• Defining technical and safety requirements for the transport of dangerous goods and ensuring compliance with ADR principles and applicable regulations.

• Specific operations by using customised equipment, analysing related working procedures and Safety assessments.

• Developing technical specifications, work procedures and contract documentation for transport and handling activities.

• Supervising contractor activities on site, ensuring Safety during the operations in both conventional and radioactive environments.

• Collaborating with the EN-THE design office to develop custom handling tools and conduct logistic studies.

• Collaborating with Radiation Protection Services to establish/redact the Work Dose Planning and Radiological work permit (DIMR).

• Performing handling operations in specific situations.

Bachelor's degree or equivalent relevant experience in the field of Logistics, Mechanics or Electromechanics or a related field.
 ADR certificate would be an additional asset. Driving and operator licences for electrical overhead travelling cranes, industrial trucks, mobile elevating platforms, etc would be an additional asset.
 Experience:

• Extensive experience in heavy handling and transport operations.

• Proven experience in worksite logistics.

• Proven experience in technical contract supervision.

• Proven experience of work in a radioactive environment will be an asset.

• Basic knowledge of remote-handling systems.

• A thorough understanding of the principles of ADR regulations in order to identify, interpret and communicate the requirements applicable to the transport of dangerous goods would be an asset.
 Technical competencies:

• Operation and maintenance of lifting and handling equipment.

• Operation and maintenance of transport systems.

• Definition and installation of transport systems.

• Transport of dangerous goods.
 Behavioural competencies:

• Achieving Results: delivering high quality work on time and fulfilling expectations.

• Demonstrating Flexibility: adapting quickly and resourcefully to shifting priorities and requirements.

• Solving Problems: anticipating obstacles; assessing alternative solutions in order to have a fall-back plan.

• Working in Teams: working well in groups and readily fitting into a team; participating fully and taking an active role in team activities.

• Working in the Interest of the Organization: following rules and regulations and encouraging others to do the same.
 Language skills:
 Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.

 This vacancy will be filled as soon as possible, and applications should normally reach us no later than 18.10.2026 at 23:59 CEST .
 Employment Conditions

 Working Hours: 40 hours per week
 Job Flexibility: Fully Onsite
 This position involves:

• Participation in a regular stand-by duty, including nights, Sundays and official holidays.

• Work in Radiation Areas.

• Interventions in underground installations.

• A valid driving licence.

• Work during nights, Sundays and official holidays, when required by the needs of the Organization.

• Shift work, when required by the needs of the Organization.

• Stand-by duty, when required by the needs of the Organization.
 Job grade: 4-5
 Job reference: EN-THE-HH-2026-196-LD
 Field of work: Mechanical Engineering
 Benchmark Job Title: Mechanical Technical Engineer

Global Benefits

• A competitive salary (tax free), increasing in line with your years of relevant experience.

• 30 days of paid leave per year plus 2 weeks annual closure.

• Coverage by CERN’s comprehensive health insurance scheme (for yourself, your spouse and children), and membership of the CERN Pension Fund.

• Family, child and infant monthly allowances depending on your individual circumstances.

descriptionByLocale.it:
Introduzione
Il Dipartimento di Ingegneria (EN) fornisce al CERN le competenze di Ingegneria, Sistemi di Infrastrutture e Coordinamento Tecnico necessarie per la progettazione, l'installazione, il funzionamento, la manutenzione e lo smontaggio delle fasi del complesso acceleratore CERN e delle sue strutture sperimentali.

La posizione è all'interno del Gruppo di Ingegneria dei Trasporti e della Gestione (EN-THE), responsabile della preparazione, organizzazione e coordinamento di tutte le operazioni di trasporto e gestione per gli acceleratori e gli esperimenti del CERN. Il Gruppo gestisce anche il trasporto di migliaia di articoli convenzionali e non convenzionali, prodotti chimici e radioattivi ogni anno.

In qualità di Transport and Handling Specialist in EN-THE, sarete parte della sezione Heavy Handling (EN-HE-HH), che è responsabile per l'organizzazione e la supervisione delle operazioni di trasporto, movimentazione e sollevamento presso gli acceleratori CERN complessi, aree sperimentali e edifici industriali sia in sotterraneo che in locali superficiali.
Funzioni
In qualità di Transport and Handling Specialist nella sezione EN-THE-HH, sarai parte di un team di 10 persone (ingegnere tecnico e tecnico) incaricato di:

• Coordinamento delle operazioni di trasporto e movimentazione per il complesso Accelerator, Esperimenti e locali superficiali.

• Riunioni di coordinamento e pianificazione per valutare le esigenze tecniche e di risorse.

• Valutare e proporre possibili soluzioni di movimentazione e trasporto.

• Definire i requisiti tecnici e di sicurezza per il trasporto di merci pericolose e garantire il rispetto dei principi ADR e delle normative applicabili.

• Operazioni specifiche utilizzando attrezzature personalizzate, analisi relative procedure di lavoro e valutazioni di sicurezza.

• Sviluppo di specifiche tecniche, procedure di lavoro e documentazione contrattuale per le attività di trasporto e gestione.

• Supervisione delle attività degli appaltatori in loco, garantire la sicurezza durante le operazioni in ambienti convenzionali e radioattivi.

• Collaborando con l'ufficio di progettazione EN-THE per sviluppare strumenti di gestione personalizzati e condurre studi logistici.

• Collaborando con i Servizi di Protezione delle Radiazioni per stabilire/risolvere il permesso di lavoro Dose Planning e Radiological work (DIMR).

• Eseguire operazioni di gestione in situazioni specifiche.

Corso di laurea o equivalente esperienza rilevante nel campo della logistica, Meccanica o Elettromeccanica o un campo relativo.
Il certificato ADR sarebbe un'ulteriore risorsa. Le licenze di guida e di operatore per gru da viaggio elettriche, camion industriali, piattaforme mobili di elevazione, ecc sarebbero un ulteriore vantaggio.
Esperienza:

• Ampia esperienza nelle operazioni di trasporto e movimentazione pesanti.

• Esperienza dimostrata nella logistica del cantiere.

• Esperienza comprovata nella supervisione dei contratti tecnici.

• La comprovata esperienza di lavoro in un ambiente radioattivo sarà un bene.

• Conoscenza di base dei sistemi di gestione remota.

• Una comprensione approfondita dei principi della normativa ADR al fine di identificare, interpretare e comunicare i requisiti applicabili al trasporto di merci pericolose sarebbe un bene.
Competenze tecniche:

descriptionByLocale.en:
Introduction
The Engineering Department (EN) provides CERN with the Engineering expertise, Infrastructure Systems and Technical Coordination necessary for the design, installation, operation, maintenance and dismantling phases of the CERN accelerator complex and its experimental facilities.

The position is within the Transport and Handling Engineering Group (EN-THE), responsible for preparing, organising and coordinating all transport and handling operations for the CERN accelerators and experiments. The Group also manages the transport of thousands of conventional and unconventional items, chemical and radioactive products each year.

As a Transport and Handling Specialist in EN-THE, you will be part of the Heavy Handling (EN-HE-HH) Section, which is in charge for organising and supervising transport, handling and lifting operations at CERNs accelerators complex, experimental areas and industrial buildings both underground and in surface premises.
Functions
As a Transport and Handling Specialist in the EN-THE-HH Section, you will be part of a team of 10 people (technical engineers and technicians) in charge of:

• Coordinating transport and handling operations for the Accelerator complex, Experiments, and surface premises.

• Coordinating and planning meetings to evaluate technical and resource needs.

• Assessing and proposing possible handling and transport solutions.

• Defining technical and safety requirements for the transport of dangerous goods and ensuring compliance with ADR principles and applicable regulations.

• Specific operations by using customised equipment, analysing related working procedures and Safety assessments.

• Developing technical specifications, work procedures and contract documentation for transport and handling activities.

• Supervising contractor activities on site, ensuring Safety during the operations in both conventional and radioactive environments.

• Collaborating with the EN-THE design office to develop custom handling tools and conduct logistic studies.

• Collaborating with Radiation Protection Services to establish/redact the Work Dose Planning and Radiological work permit (DIMR).

• Performing handling operations in specific situations.

Bachelor's degree or equivalent relevant experience in the field of Logistics, Mechanics or Electromechanics or a related field.
ADR certificate would be an additional asset. Driving and operator licences for electrical overhead travelling cranes, industrial trucks, mobile elevating platforms, etc would be an additional asset.
Experience:

• Extensive experience in heavy handling and transport operations.

• Proven experience in worksite logistics.

• Proven experience in technical contract supervision.

• Proven experience of work in a radioactive environment will be an asset.

• Basic knowledge of remote-handling systems.

• A thorough understanding of the principles of ADR regulations in order to identify, interpret and communicate the requirements applicable to the transport of dangerous goods would be an asset.
Technical competencies:

• Operation and maintenance of lifting and handling equipment.

• Operation and maintenance of transport systems.

• Definition and installation of transport systems.

• Transport of dangerous goods.
Behavioural competencies:

• Achieving Results: delivering high quality work on time and fulfilling expectations.

• Demonstrating Flexibility: adapting quickly and resourcefully to shifting priorities and requirements.

• Solving Problems: anticipating obstacles; assessing alternative solutions in order to have a fall-back plan.

• Working in Teams: working well in groups and readily fitting into a team; participating fully and taking an active role in team activities.

• Working in the Interest of the Organization: following rules and regulations and encouraging others to do the same.
Language skills:
Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.

Eligibility and closing date:
Diversity has been an integral part of CERN's mission since its foundation and is an established value of the Organization. Employing a diverse workforce is central to our success. We welcome applications from all Member States and Associate Member States .
This vacancy will be filled as soon as possible, and applications should normally reach us no later than 18.10.2026 at 23:59 CEST .
Employment Conditions
Contract type: Limited duration contract (5 years). Subject to certain conditions, holders of limited-duration contracts may apply for an indefinite position.
Working Hours: 40 hours per week
Job Flexibility: Fully Onsite
This position involves:

• Participation in a regular stand-by duty, including nights, Sundays and official holidays.

• Work in Radiation Areas.

• Interventions in underground installations.

• A valid driving licence.

• Work during nights, Sundays and official holidays, when required by the needs of the Organization.

• Shift work, when required by the needs of the Organization.

• Stand-by duty, when required by the needs of the Organization.
Job grade: 4-5
Job reference: EN-THE-HH-2026-196-LD
Field of work: Mechanical Engineering
Benchmark Job Title: Mechanical Technical Engineer

Global Benefits

• A competitive salary (tax free), increasing in line with your years of relevant experience.

• 30 days of paid leave per year plus 2 weeks annual closure.

• Coverage by CERN’s comprehensive health insurance scheme (for yourself, your spouse and children), and membership of the CERN Pension Fund.

• Family, child and infant monthly allowances depending on your individual circumstances.

• A relocation package (installation grant, removal, travel expenses) depending on your individual circumstances.

• Possibility to extend your contract up to 8 years + eligibility for indefinite contract tenure.
Overview of CERN - Discover a world where the impossible is made possible!
At CERN, the European Organization for Nuclear Research, we are pushing the frontiers of science and technology. Our groundbreaking work brings together not only physicists but also a diverse range of professionals from engineering, technical, scientific, and administrative fields. Together, we foster an environment where innovation and collaboration thrive.
Every day, we face exciting new challenges and opportunities to contribute to cutting-edge research that shapes our understanding of the universe. We meet these challenges through the diverse perspectives within our teams, ensuring every contribution is valued and driving our shared sense of inclusion and purpose. Diversity is a core value of CERN since its foundation, and it remains central to our mission and continued success.
If you are ready to be part of a dynamic, inclusive community pushing the boundaries of knowledge, CERN is the place where your curiosity and skills can thrive. Be part of our mission to uncover what lies at the heart of the universe! TAKE PART!

Die Ingenieurabteilung (EN) stellt dem CERN die technische Expertise, Infrastruktursysteme und technische Koordination zur Verfügung, die für die Planungs-, Installations-, Betriebs-, Wartungs- und Demontagephasen des CERN-Beschleunigerkomplexes und seiner Versuchsanlagen erforderlich sind.

Die Position ist innerhalb der Transport and Handling Engineering Group (EN-THE), die für die Vorbereitung, Organisation und Koordination aller Transport- und Umschlagvorgänge für die CERN-Beschleuniger und Experimente verantwortlich ist. Die Gruppe verwaltet auch den Transport von Tausenden von konventionellen und unkonventionellen Artikeln, chemischen und radioaktiven Produkten pro Jahr.

Als Transport- und Handling-Spezialist in EN-THE sind Sie Teil der Sektion Schweres Handling (EN-HE-HH), die für die Organisation und Überwachung von Transport-, Handling- und Hebevorgängen in CERN-Beschleunigerkomplexen, Versuchsgebieten und Industriegebäuden sowohl unterirdisch als auch in Oberflächengebäuden zuständig ist.
Funktionen
Als Transport- und Umschlagspezialist in der Sektion EN-THE-HH sind Sie Teil eines Teams von 10 Personen (Techniker und Techniker) verantwortlich für:

• Koordinierende Transport- und Handhabungsvorgänge für den Accelerator-Komplex, Experimente und Oberflächenräume.

• Koordination und Planung von Meetings zur Bewertung des technischen und Ressourcenbedarfs.

• Bewertung und Vorschlag möglicher Handhabungs- und Transportlösungen.

• Entwicklung technischer Spezifikationen, Arbeitsverfahren und Vertragsunterlagen für Transport- und Abfertigungstätigkeiten.

• Überwachung der Tätigkeiten der Auftragnehmer vor Ort, Gewährleistung der Sicherheit während des Betriebs in konventionellen und radioaktiven Umgebungen.

• Zusammenarbeit mit dem EN-THE Designbüro, um maßgeschneiderte Handhabungswerkzeuge zu entwickeln und logistische Studien durchzuführen.

• Zusammenarbeit mit Radiation Protection Services, um die Arbeitsdosisplanung und radiologische Arbeitserlaubnis (DIMR) zu erstellen / zu bearbeiten.

• Durchführung von Handhabungsvorgängen in bestimmten Situationen.

Bachelor-Abschluss oder gleichwertige einschlägige Erfahrung im Bereich der Logistik, Mechanik oder Elektromechanik oder einem verwandten Bereich.

• Nachgewiesene Erfahrung in der Baustellenlogistik.

• Nachgewiesene Erfahrung in der technischen Auftragsüberwachung.

• Bewährte Erfahrung in der Arbeit in einer radioaktiven Umgebung wird ein Gewinn sein.

• Grundkenntnisse über Fernbedienungssysteme.

Technische Kompetenzen:

• Betrieb und Wartung von Transportsystemen.

• Definition und Installation von Transportsystemen.

• Beförderung gefährlicher Güter.
Verhaltenskompetenzen:

Englisch gesprochen und geschrieben, mit der Verpflichtung, Französisch zu lernen.

jobs.description:
You will join one of CERN’s theoretical physics research groups, if selected for this Research Fellowship, to develop and lead your own research programme at the frontier of fundamental physics. You will work in a highly collaborative and international environment, contributing to the development of theoretical models, performing analytical and computational research, and advancing the understanding of particle physics and related fields.
 You will also be part of CERN’s vibrant scientific community through seminars, workshops, training activities and collaborative projects.

Sie werden einer der Forschungsgruppen des CERN für theoretische Physik beitreten, wenn Sie für dieses Forschungsstipendium ausgewählt werden, um Ihr eigenes Forschungsprogramm an der Grenze der Grundlagenphysik zu entwickeln und zu leiten. Sie arbeiten in einem hochgradig kooperativen und internationalen Umfeld, tragen zur Entwicklung theoretischer Modelle bei, führen analytische und computergestützte Forschung durch und fördern das Verständnis der Teilchenphysik und verwandter Bereiche.
Sie werden auch Teil der lebendigen wissenschaftlichen Gemeinschaft des CERN durch Seminare, Workshops, Schulungsaktivitäten und Kooperationsprojekte sein.
Ihre wichtigsten Aufgaben

• Sie forschen in der theoretischen Physik.

• Sie tragen zum theoretischen Physikprogramm des CERN bei, indem Sie innovative theoretische Ansätze entwickeln und die Interpretation experimenteller Ergebnisse vorantreiben.

• Sie arbeiten mit theoretischen und experimentellen Physikern an der Forschung im Zusammenhang mit der Teilchenphysik und grundlegenden Wechselwirkungen zusammen.

• Sie entwickeln und verfolgen eigene Forschungsinteressen im Rahmen des Fellowships.
Dein Profil

• Sie haben einen PhD in theoretischer Physik oder haben eine geplante PhD Verteidigung, bevor Sie Ihren Termin am CERN aufnehmen.

• Sie haben nicht mehr als sechs Jahre Forschungserfahrung nach Abschluss Ihrer PhD.

• Sie haben einen starken Hintergrund in der theoretischen Teilchenphysik oder einem eng verwandten Gebiet.

• Sie haben Forschungserfahrung, die mit den wissenschaftlichen Aktivitäten in der Theorieabteilung des CERN übereinstimmt.

• Sie sind motiviert, sich einem führenden internationalen Forschungsumfeld anzuschließen und zu einer einflussreichen wissenschaftlichen Forschung beizutragen.

• Sie sind bestrebt, Ihre eigenen Forschungsinteressen im Rahmen des Fellowship zu entwickeln und zu verfolgen.
Ihre Fähigkeiten

• Sie haben starke analytische und Problemlösungsfähigkeiten im Kontext der theoretischen Physik.

• Sie können in großen, internationalen wissenschaftlichen Teams zusammenarbeiten.

• Sie kommunizieren effektiv in einem wissenschaftlichen Umfeld, einschließlich der Präsentation und Diskussion von Forschungsergebnissen.

• Sie können unabhängig arbeiten und gleichzeitig zu gemeinsamen Forschungszielen und Verbundprojekten beitragen.

jobs.title: Mechanical Technician for CMS (EP-CMS-IC-2026-226-GRAE)
jobs.description:
We are recruiting two early-career graduates for Mechanical Technician positions within the CMS experiment. Both positions involve hands-on mechanical work and close collaboration with technicians, engineers, and physicists, but each will have a different main area of responsibility.
 One position will join the Electromagnetic Calorimeter (ECAL) team, supporting the refurbishment of the barrel electromagnetic calorimeter and covering a large panel of activities and responsibilities, from mechanical work and the handling and assembly of detector parts to logistic activities.
 The second position will join the CMS Technical Coordination crew, supporting mechanical activities for the CMS detector and its infrastructure, including maintenance, upgrades, tooling, and heavy-lifting operations.
 Your responsibilities
 Key Tasks ECAL position:

• Participate in the extraction and insertion of the ECAL supermodules, including the preparation, installation, and removal of the required tooling.

• Carry out mechanical operations during the refurbishment of the supermodules, including the replacement of cooling fittings.

• Support the installation of ECAL services and electronics and assist with related logistics.
 Key tasks Technical Coordination position:

• Participate in mechanical work for the upgrade, maintenance, and repair of the CMS detector and its associated infrastructure.

• Manufacture mechanical parts and contribute to on-site assembly, installation, alignment, and repair activities.

• Support the development of tooling and the preparation or modification of technical drawings using drafting software such as CATIA.

• Participate in heavy-lifting and movement operations using equipment such as strand jacks, air pads, and hydraulic jacks, and support regular checks and maintenance of this equipment.
 Your profile

• Initial hands-on experience in the construction and assembly of mechanical components and structures.

• Experience in mechanical equipment or detector assembly, including cooling connections, pressure testing, or leak detection.

• Experience using machine tools and hand tools for mechanical manufacturing activities.

• Experience with mechanical systems and the handling of large, heavy, or fragile equipment.

• Experience with drafting software, such as CATIA.
 Skills

• Knowledge of manufacturing techniques for mechanical parts.

• Experience in the assembly and integration of mechanical structures, equipment, and systems.

• Knowledge of the operation and maintenance of cooling-water systems.

• Experience in the safe operation of mechanical handling systems and the application of safety procedures related to heavy machinery and mechanical operations.

• Problem-solving skills and attention to detail.

• Ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team.

• Clear communication skills and the ability to follow technical instructions accurately.

• Spoken and written English or French, with a commitment to learn the other language.
 Eligibility criteria:

• You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State .

• By the application deadline, you have a maximum of two years of professional experience since graduation in Mechanics or related (or a related field) and your highest educational qualification is a general secondary education diploma .

• You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.

• Applicants with a Bachelor's, Master's or PhD degree are not eligible.

Job closing date: 12.10.2026 at 23:59 CEST.
 Contract duration: 24 months, with a possible extension up to 36 months maximum.
 Working hours: 40 hours per week
 Job flexibility: Fully Onsite
 Target start date: 01-December-2026
 This position involves:

• Work in Radiation Areas.

• Interventions in underground installations.

• Residence in the immediate vicinity of the Organization's installations.

• A valid driving licence.

• Work during nights, Sundays and official holidays, when required by the needs of the Organization.

• For the ECAL position: Exposure to risk of falling from heights during scaffolding assembly and dismantling operations.

• For the ECAL position: Exposure to electromagnetic fields under certain conditions.
 Job reference: EP-CMS-IC-2026-226-GRAE
 Field of work: Mechanical Engineering
 Benchmark job: 300090 - Mechanical Technician

Global Benefits

• A monthly stipend of 4687 Swiss Francs per month (tax free).

• 30 days of paid leave per year plus 2 weeks annual closure.

• Coverage by CERN’s comprehensive health insurance scheme (for yourself, your spouse and children), and membership of the CERN Pension Fund.

 Overview of CERN - Discover a world where the impossible is made possible!
 At CERN, the European Organization for Nuclear Research, we are pushing the frontiers of science and technology. Our groundbreaking work brings together not only physicists but also a diverse range of professionals from engineering, technical, scientific, and administrative fields. Together, we foster an environment where innovation and collaboration thrive.
 Every day, we face exciting new challenges and opportunities to contribute to cutting-edge research that shapes our understanding of the universe. We meet these challenges through the diverse perspectives within our teams, ensuring every contribution is valued and driving our shared sense of inclusion and purpose. Diversity is a core value of CERN since its foundation, and it remains central to our mission and continued success.
